subject: CargoLoop throughput profile and next steps (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@cargoloop.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: CargoLoop throughput profile and next steps (post-discovery)

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and a compact list of asks so we can finalize a sizing recommendation: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use: real-time fulfillment assistant embedded in web checkout and an async batch enrichment job for post-order summarization.
- Real-time path: average user session 2–3 prompts, streaming responses for the assistant (partial tokens streamed).
- Batch path: nightly processing of ~200k orders/day, larger token payloads per order.
- Latency target for real-time: p99 <= 350ms for initial token generation; acceptable p95 <= 120ms.

Open items / what we need from you:
1) Sample payloads (JSON or CSV) representing typical requests for both real-time and batch. Include average and 95th token counts.
2) Peak vs steady-state QPS estimate (e.g., peak 10-minute crest, average over hour).
3) Concurrency expectations for streaming sessions (how many simultaneous streaming connections at peak).
4) Any existing logs/traces showing request size distribution or tail latency spikes.
5) Confirm whether the streaming client expects chunked partial tokens (we'll need to pick streaming protocol settings).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Karthik will draft a rough capacity estimate and recommended trial configuration (batch size, quantization profile, and target throughput).
- We'll propose a short tech deep-dive (30–45m) to validate assumptions and schedule a 1-hour load test window if you can provide opt-in test traffic.

Suggested timeline: please share the sample payloads and QPS numbers by EOD 2025-04-04 so we can deliver an initial sizing by 2025-04-06.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: [sla-draft-Redwood-v1.docx] (draft SLA for review)
From: Alex Ruiz <alex@cargoloop.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@cargoloop.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CargoLoop throughput profile and next steps (post-discovery)

Thanks Marissa — solid summary, appreciate the clarity. Answers below inline.

Quick answers:
- Sample payloads: attaching a small CSV ('sample_payloads.csv') with 200 rows (mix of realtime and batch). Columns: request_id, path (real_time|batch), tokens_input, tokens_output_est, user_agent.
- Peak vs steady: typical steady-state for real-time is ~18 QPS across our US checkout peak window (9–10am PT). We see short crests during marketing spikes up to ~140 QPS for 3–7 minutes. Nightly batch runs produce an average of 2.4k RPS equivalent when translated to tokens/sec but these are non-latency sensitive.
- Concurrency for streaming: expect up to ~65 concurrent streaming sessions during peak crest.
- Logs/traces: we can share a redacted tail-sample showing request size distribution (will send as a zipped csv if needed).
- Streaming: yes, client expects chunked partial tokens; we use a chunk size ~256 tokens on client side.

Latency target confirmations: p99 target for initial token generation <= 350ms (hard), p95 <= 120ms (soft). For batch, latency not applicable.

We are OK to provide opt-in test traffic for a short window. Procurement copied.

—Alex
Alex Ruiz | Head of Platform Engineering, CargoLoop
alex@cargoloop.com

Attachment: [sample_payloads.csv]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@cargoloop.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CargoLoop throughput profile and next steps (technical notes)

Alex — thanks for the fast turn. A few technical clarifying questions that will materially shift sizing estimates: 

1) For the real-time assistant, can you give a per-prompt average and 95th percentile for tokens_input AND tokens_output_est? The CSV helps, but we'll need the percentiles to choose batching windows.
2) For the 140 QPS crest: is that 140 separate new requests/sec or does it include re-requests/edits from the client? Are sessions sticky (same user opens multiple streaming channels)?
3) For streaming concurrency: are those long-lived connections (~30+ seconds) or short (under 5s)? This determines memory/KV cache sizing.
4) Do you have a percent of requests that request tool calls or function calls (structured outputs)? Those change decoding time.

Initial sizing thought (very rough): For p99 <= 350ms on initial token at 140 QPS crest with 65 concurrent streaming sessions and avg 60 tokens out, we'll likely recommend a two-tier approach in the trial: a small dedicated pool for steady-state and a burst-capable shared pool for cranking through crests. I can sketch numbers once we have the token distributions.

If you prefer, let's schedule a 30-minute tech deep-dive tomorrow (2025-04-04) at 10:00am PT to go through the CSV live. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/mtg/5f8b-2c3a

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Performance Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Ruiz <alex@cargoloop.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CargoLoop throughput profile and next steps (technical notes)

Karthik — thanks. Quick clarifications: 
- Per-prompt percentiles included in the attached CSV: tokens_input (avg=42, p95=128), tokens_output_est (avg=58, p95=210) for realtime. Batch average tokens_output_est ~1,400.
- The 140 QPS crest is new requests/sec; some are retry traffic (~5–8%) but not substantial.
- Streaming connections are typically 8–20s (most are shorter than 30s) but do occupy an open socket for the duration.
- Tool calls: ~6% of requests trigger server-side tool calls (structured outputs).

We can do the tech deep-dive tomorrow at 10:00am PT — Elena (cc'd) will send a calendar invite and include a shared S3 link for traces.

—Alex
